clue.text: Sacrificial rabbits as portrayed by Rembrandt?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, poor batsmen (rabbits) sent in late in the day to protect better ones, sacrificing their wickets
Rembrandt's famous painting The Night Watch shows a company of civic guardsmen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbits' is cricket slang for weak batsmen; a NIGHTWATCHMAN is a lower-order batsman sent in near the close of play to shield a better one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: cricket's sacrificial late-evening batsmen, and the guardsmen painted in Rembrandt's The Night Watch.

clue.text: Islander excited to be on vacations

indicators.note: being excited stirs these letters up into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone from an island gets thrilled at the thought of going on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited to be' signals rearranging the eleven letters of ON VACATIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Cape Breton Island belongs to the Canadian province, so counts as an islander there.

clue.text: Port's good -—- really good when laid up

indicators.note: in a down clue, laid up means set upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1, written A ONE, means first-rate

explanation.surface: Someone praises a port, insisting it is excellent when it is stored away to age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid up' reverses A ONE to give ENOA after G. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is a major Italian seaport on the Ligurian coast.

clue.text: Excellent means of access to attic

definitions.meaning: the uppermost set of stairs in a house, leading to the loft

explanation.definitionFit: Top-class quality is one sense; the literal uppermost staircase climbing to the loft is the other.

clue.text: Failure to recall men stupidly invading East

indicators.note: invading means getting inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: the East, the Orient, is Asia

indicators.note: acting stupidly suggests the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A forgetful episode: some foolish men barge into Asia and can't remember why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East' as Asia is a crossword staple: the Orient. 'stupidly' and 'invading' do the work here.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is a medical loss of memory, the inability to remember.

clue.text: European's method of payment or audit, say

indicators.note: say signals a word judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: a cheque is a way to pay and a check is an audit; both are pronounced the same

explanation.surface: A European asks whether to pay by cheque or have the accounts checked.
explanation.walkthrough: Either CHEQUE (payment) or CHECK (audit) gives the sound; 'say' points to the soundalike CZECH. 'European's' is European is.
explanation.definitionFit: A Czech is a person from the Czech Republic in central Europe.

clue.text: Eccentric that is encountered in strange dream

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are made odd, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something eccentric turns up inside an odd dream, as in Wonderland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' scrambles both words; 'is encountered in' pictures one jumbled word sitting inside the other, and the clue as a whole nods to Alice's dreamlike Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mad Hatter of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland has become a byword for a wildly odd person.

clue.text: Japanese acts on wife's present

parts.note: No (or Noh) is classical Japanese masked drama

explanation.surface: A gift from a wife includes tickets to Japanese theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wife's' is wife has; 'on' places W after NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Now means the present moment, the time at hand.

clue.text: A hot place, like Aix?

parts.note: the southern French spa town is known by a longer name, and a hot spot sits inside the last word of that full title

explanation.surface: Aix in southern France is a scorching spot.
explanation.walkthrough: An indirect hidden word: Aix is Aix-en-Provence, and the answer sits in the middle of its final word.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is a chamber heated for baking, the hottest spot in a kitchen.

clue.text: Clearly defined and fixed on canvas, perhaps

definitions.meaning: held to the mat in wrestling, or a tent fixed with pegs; canvas is a wrestling ring floor

explanation.definitionFit: To be precisely established is one sense; to be held fast to the mat by a wrestler is the other.

clue.text: People in republic throwing king back in river

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: the Isis is the stretch of the Thames at Oxford

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: Citizens of a republic toss a monarch into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is Oxford's name for the Thames. 'back' turns the king round; 'throwing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Israelis are citizens of the State of Israel, a parliamentary republic.

clue.text: US newspaperman is informed about Times leader

parts.note: to hear about something is to be told of it

indicators.note: a leader is what comes first, the opening letter of the word Times

explanation.surface: An American press baron is told about the Times editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' also means a newspaper editorial, a neat touch beside 'Times'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Randolph Hearst built the largest American newspaper empire.

clue.text: Vehicles followed by another into theatre

parts.note: stages are stagecoaches
another vehicle, a lorry

explanation.surface: Coaches followed by a lorry drive into a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' means keen on, so 'into theatre' is the definition, not an instruction to put something inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dazzled by and longing for a life on the stage is being enthusiastic about drama.

clue.text: Carol I sang badly, as alto member of family

indicators.note: singing badly means the letters come out wrong, rearranged

explanation.surface: A carol sung poorly by an alto in the family choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges CAROL I SANG; 'as' is a link. The family is the oboe family, of which the cor anglais is the alto member.
explanation.definitionFit: The cor anglais is a deeper oboe, the alto voice of the double-reed family.

clue.text: Disposed of lots of uranium, carried out, kept outside

indicators.note: the second word stays outside, enclosing the first piece

parts.note: actioned means dealt with, carried out
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A stock of uranium was dealt with and stored outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept outside' means ACTIONED encloses U.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling goods in lots to the highest bidder is sale by auction.

clue.text: Maintains a position — it's time, in a sense

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone holds their ground, feeling the time has come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the apostrophe word and the time abbreviation inside the sense, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit tight is to stay put and not change one's stance.

clue.text: Hazard when driving a two-wheeler

definitions.meaning: a light two-wheeled carriage drawn by a pony

explanation.walkthrough: 'when driving' joins the halves and hints at golf (a bunker is a sand hazard) and at driving a pony carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare is a pitfall, and a pony-drawn light carriage on two wheels is the other meaning.

clue.text: Old record is covered with new backing

indicators.note: is is covered by the other piece, so it goes inside
backing means set going backwards

parts.note: CD, the compact ..., is the new form of record

explanation.surface: A vintage record has a new lining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns CD into DC, which surrounds IS. 'new' stands for the newer kind of record beside the old one.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc, the vinyl gramophone record, is the older format a CD replaced.

clue.text: Pursue leaderless country to have real discussions

indicators.note: the first letter, the leader, is lost

parts.note: to stalk is to pursue
Turkey is a country

explanation.surface: A hunter tracks a nation lacking a leader before negotiating seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' drops the S from STALK; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking turkey is an idiom for getting down to frank, business-like discussion.

clue.text: Valiant constituents of a recently liberated state

indicators.note: the letters are the components of a word, rearranged into another

explanation.surface: The brave voters of a newly freed country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' rearranges VALIANT; the state is Latvia, independent from the Soviet Union in 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvian is the adjective for Latvia, which regained independence when the Soviet Union broke up.

clue.text: Disheartened environmental foot-soldier, member of green group

indicators.note: losing the heart, all the middle, leaving only the opening and closing letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A dispirited eco-warrior belongs to the Greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' strips the whole middle from ENVIRONMENTAL FOOT-SOLDIER, keeping ENV and IER. 'green' wants to mean ecological, given 'environmental'; it is envious.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is a colour of jealousy, and the green-eyed group are those who envy.

clue.text: What's concerning expert? It's a copy!

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the expert's view is, and finds it's merely a copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A repro is a reproduction, an imitation of an original.

clue.text: A line I used, swallowed by attractive women as a whole

indicators.note: being swallowed means being taken inside

parts.note: totty is British slang for attractive women

explanation.surface: A chat-up line is used on attractive women, and they lap it all up.
explanation.walkthrough: Totty is British slang for attractive women. 'swallowed by' takes in the three pieces; 'used' and 'as a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Totality means the entire amount, everything taken together.

clue.text: How one scores slowly or fast — at Oval

parts.note: Lent is the season of fasting
O is an oval shape

explanation.surface: A cricketer scores slowly or quickly at the Oval ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, so 'scores' wants to mean runs; it is a musical score. 'or' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is a musical direction marking a passage to be played slowly.

clue.text: Chief motive, as result of early graduation?

definitions.meaning: the main driving force behind something
a master's degree gained in the springtime, read as a phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as MA IN SPRING, a degree taken early in the year.
explanation.definitionFit: The main motivating force is named after the central coiled spring that drives a watch.

clue.text: Annoyed left, right, and centre? Bother!

indicators.note: the leftmost letter of the word, its first
the rightmost letter of the word, its last
the centre is the middle letter of the seven

explanation.surface: Someone irritated on every side exclaims in exasperation.
explanation.walkthrough: Annoyed gives its leftmost, rightmost and central letters in that order: A, D, O. 'left, right and centre' also means everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or trouble, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Part of speech negating international group

parts.note: no is a word that negates
UN is the United Nations

explanation.surface: A grammatical term rejects an international body.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun is one of the grammatical word classes, naming things.

clue.text: Social support system bringing gain in bloody awful job

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
awful means the letters are a mess, rearranged

parts.note: work is a job
net is a gain, profit

explanation.surface: Friends from school help someone get ahead in a terrible job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloody' looks like an intensifier but is the anagram fodder for 'awful'; 'in' sets the gain between the two parts. 'bringing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual help among former pupils of the same school is a network of patronage.
